body.working_title: Bias, efficiency and consistency of ETS smoothing-parameter estimates: smooth vs statsforecast

body.name: Ivan Svetunkov
body.words: Ivan Svetunkov, ORCID 0000-0001-7826-0281. I am the guarantor and the supervisor of this study.

body.text: How well do smooth (ES) and statsforecast (AutoETS, fixed form) estimate the smoothing parameters alpha, beta, gamma of the ETS model that generated simulated data: bias, efficiency (RMSE, MAE) and consistency as the series length grows?

smooth.ES (Python, v1.2.0), the package default: initial='backcasting', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual', model form fixed; initial states obtained by backcasting, not optimised.

body.text: Pilot RN1 (R=10, all 20 cells, exploratory) took 22.6 CPU-seconds summed over cells, so R=300 needs about 30 times that (roughly 11 CPU-minutes, about 3 minutes on 4 processes): under the 20-minute limit, so R stays 300. The pilot had no failures; it was used only to check the script and timing, not to choose thresholds or settings.

Comparability, fixed before the confirmatory run. (1) Parametrisation: both packages use the single-source-of-error (innovations) form with additive error, l_t = l_{t-1} + alpha e_t, b_t = b_{t-1} + beta e_t, s_t = s_{t-m} + gamma e_t, so alpha, beta, gamma are the same quantities as in the data-generating equations and no conversion is applied (statsforecast follows forecast::ets, where beta is the trend persistence on the error, not the Holt beta*; smooth's persistence vector is the same g). (2) Initial states: smooth optimised (initial='optimal') and statsforecast (optimised) are the comparable pair; smooth backcasting (initial='backcasting', smooth's default) is a separate arm. (3) Loss: both maximise the Gaussian likelihood (smooth loss='likelihood'; statsforecast ets: -2 log likelihood); statsforecast optimises with Nelder-Mead, smooth with its NLopt optimiser. (4) Bounds: smooth bounds='usual' (0<=alpha,beta,gamma<=1, beta<=alpha, gamma<=1-alpha); statsforecast bounds 'both' (box [1e-4, 0.9999] plus usual and admissibility checks). The bounds are close but not identical; estimates within 1e-3 of a bound (0 or 1 for alpha, 0 or alpha for beta, 0 or 1-alpha for gamma) are counted as bound hits. Neither API exposes a convergence flag that the script reads: failures are errors, non-finite estimates, or a changed model form; non-convergence is only visible as bound hits and warnings (counted).

body.design: One run of claimset-code/ets-param-estimation/sim.py --R 300 --seed 2026 (base seed 2026; replicate seed = SeedSequence([2026, process-set index, T, replicate])). Processes: ETS(A,N,N) alpha=0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) (alpha,beta)=(0.3,0.05) and (0.5,0.2); ETS(A,N,A) m=12 (alpha,gamma)=(0.2,0.1); innovations form, N(0,1) errors, l0=100, b0=1, s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12), no burn-in. T in {50,100,250,500}, R=300 replicates per cell (20 cells). Each series is fitted with three arms, model form fixed to the generating form: smooth ES optimised initial states, smooth ES backcasting (default), statsforecast AutoETS; all with Gaussian likelihood. Comparability as in decision DC1. R stays 300 because the pilot RN1 shows the full run is far below 20 minutes.
body.analysis: Per arm x cell x parameter over replicates that did not fail: bias (mean of estimate minus true, with 90% interval from the standard error), RMSE, MAE; failures, bound hits and warned fits counted and reported. Failed replicates are excluded from that arm's error statistics only and reported as counts. H1: share of (arm, process-set, parameter) series (24) whose RMSE at T=500 is below that at T=50. H2: share of the 32 process-set x parameter x T comparisons where smooth-optimised RMSE is below statsforecast RMSE. H3: same share for smooth-backcasting RMSE below smooth-optimised RMSE. H4-H6 (smooth optimised, smooth backcasting, statsforecast): at T=500, over all 8 parameters, the maximum of |bias| + 1.645 se (upper) and of max(0,|bias| - 1.645 se) (lower), against the bound 0.02.
